summary: Outputs TouchDesigner process performance and system-state channels such as FPS, frame time, cook/skipped-frame signals, GPU memory, active OP counts, and battery/status data.
key_concepts: Perform CHOP outputs runtime performance and system-state channels from the current TouchDesigner process.
FPS, frame time, Cook, Dropped Frames, Cook State, and Cook Realtime are diagnostics for frame pacing and skipped-frame behavior.
The Cook channel is useful when viewed through a Trail CHOP to see which frames cooked and which were skipped.
GPU, CPU memory, OP counts, perform-window focus, battery, and expression-count channels depend on hardware and platform availability.
Perform CHOP is for self-monitoring and adaptive controls; it does not optimize the network by itself.
Built-in Variables may be better than CHOP channels when an expression needs a single runtime state value.

key_params.name: msec
key_params.note: Output frame cook time in milliseconds

key_params.name: cook
key_params.note: 1 when a frame cooked, 0 when skipped

key_params.name: gputemp
key_params.note: Output NVIDIA GPU temperature when available

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: Cook time reflects the prior drawn frame, so it is a diagnostic signal rather than a predictive guarantee.
The cook channel is useful through Trail CHOP to visualize cooked versus skipped frames.
Perform CHOP is for self-monitoring and adaptive UI/control calculations; it does not optimize the network by itself.
Some system channels depend on platform/hardware availability, such as battery and GPU memory data.
Built-in Variables expose additional runtime state that may be more appropriate for expressions than CHOP channels.
